A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, retaining its core datasets and six correction methods. The complete documents, including v1 Appendices A–C and v3 Appendices A–F, are readable, and corresponding figures and tables can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 16 MLLMs, correction-method comparisons, table-extraction analysis, and choice-order experiments.

after.justification: v3 reports original QA and correction results, extends evaluation to 18 MLLMs, and adds Likert-scale consistency results and per-misleader analyses.

M1.justification: The six inference-time procedures remain unchanged, including extracted axes/tables, table-only QA using Qwen2.5-7B, and visualization redrawing with fallback to the original image. Expanded explanations and the revised flowchart do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: The original QA coverage is retained. v3 adds Lauer and O’Brien’s four matched visualization pairs, comprising eight visualizations, for Likert-scale questions. This extends task coverage from answer correctness to consistency of ratings across misleading and non-misleading presentations of identical data.

E2.justification: Gemini-1.5-flash and Gemini-1.5-pro join the main QA comparison, increasing the model set from 16 to 18. Published human results also enter CHARTOM and Likert-scale comparisons. The original models and six correction alternatives remain; ChartInstruction and Llava-Chart-Instruct refer to the same comparator.

E3.justification: Experiment 2 introduces a distinct matched-pair protocol: 18 models assign ratings from 1 to 6, with consistency assessed between presentations rather than against a ground-truth answer. Existing QA sample counts, relaxed numerical accuracy, zero-shot inference, and correction-model selection remain documented as before.

E4.justification: v3 adds diagnostic accuracy breakdowns across all 17 misleader types and comparisons with human susceptibility (Section 1.2, Figure C1). It also adds paired-rating sensitivity tests and an inverted-axis extraction failure example (Figure E2). The existing CHARTOM table-matching analysis is retained.

E5.justification: v3 introduces paired t-tests and standard deviations across model ratings for Experiment 2, and adds McNemar test statistics alongside p-values in Table D3. The three choice-shuffling seeds and corresponding mean/standard-deviation results are unchanged, moving from Table B2 to Table F4.

E6.justification: v3 adds Gemini, per-misleader, and consistency results while revising several retained-model accuracy scores and correction deltas. Table-based QA’s non-misleading p-values for Qwen2VL-7B and Ovis1.6-9B change from 0.14 and 0.07 to 0.05 each (v1 Table C3; v3 Table D3), making the reported losses significant.

T1.justification: Neither version develops theoretical results, proofs, or mathematical derivations. Table A1’s misleader definitions are retained. The added Likert-scale consistency criterion is an experimental assessment rather than a new formal theoretical development.

C1.justification: The central claims about MLLM vulnerability and inference-time mitigation remain. v3 adds a claim about inconsistent Likert-scale responses under truncated axes and explicitly asserts priority for its comprehensive assessment and correction methods, extending the stated contributions without replacing their central thesis.

C2.justification: Where v1 describes table-based QA’s non-misleading losses as non-significant, v3 recognizes significant losses and favors redrawing when preserving accuracy matters. It also explains which misleaders persist in tables, qualifies parametric-knowledge protection for recent data, and adds unequal misleader representation as a limitation.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents CHARTOM misleader-name harmonization, Google Cloud API access for Gemini, and use of Matplotlib defaults for redrawing. These are additional disclosures, not evidence that retained procedures changed. The repository link, prompt availability, and decoding settings remain.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning against human-deception research, visualization linters such as Visualint and VizLinter, table-extraction approaches beyond DePlot, and parallel MLLM studies. Its Discussion explicitly distinguishes real-world coverage and mitigation trade-offs. These cited approaches are not newly evaluated algorithmic baselines.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, Results, and Discussion are extensively rewritten. v3 adds an explicit contribution summary, organizes the evaluation around three named experiments and finer findings subsections, and reorganizes Methods and appendices. This substantially changes the narrative beyond inserting new results.

P2.justification: v3 redesigns the example montage and method flowchart, adds human reference lines to benchmark plots, and introduces Likert-scale explanatory/results figures, a misleader heatmap, an extraction example, and a dataset table. Statistical-table columns and appendix placement also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v3 improves practical guidance by discussing significant non-misleading accuracy losses from table-based QA and favoring redrawing when preservation matters, whereas v1 reported those losses as non-significant. The consistency experiment and misleader breakdown add useful diagnostic evidence. These gains are limited by the four-pair consistency sample and the abstract’s retained, overbroad claim of improving performance without compromising non-misleading accuracy.
